# .NET and Go symbol lookup

Look up declarations before inferring a counterpart. Keep symbol lookup read-only: do not edit the catalog, extract assemblies, refresh declarations, or expand the .NET package scope unless the user explicitly asks. Declarations, extraction metadata, assessments, and test identities share one maintained catalog.

## 1. Choose the right query

Run from the repository root with its Go toolchain using the independent [catalog module](../../../_catalog/go.mod), `github.com/microsoft/agent-framework-go/_catalog`. The SDK does not require or replace it. The nested module boundary excludes its tooling and data from the SDK module ZIP; the underscore prefix alone only skips package discovery. `go -C _catalog` changes the process working directory to that module: `-file` defaults to the [single catalog](../../../_catalog/dotnet-go-sdk-symbol-mapping.json) basename and `-go-root` to `..` (the SDK parent). Explicit path flags are relative to that directory or can be absolute. Start with a filtered CLI query, not a full catalog read. Substitute the requested name for the examples below.

| Need | Query |
| --- | --- |
| Recorded Go counterpart for a .NET member | `go -C _catalog run ./cmd/symbolmap mappings -assessed -symbol AIAgent.RunAsync -limit 5` |
| Recorded .NET counterparts for a Go symbol | `go -C _catalog run ./cmd/symbolmap mappings -assessed -symbol agent.Session.Get -limit 5` |
| Recorded Go-specific APIs | `go -C _catalog run ./cmd/symbolmap go-only -symbol agent. -limit 5` |
| Extracted .NET methods, whether reviewed or not | `go -C _catalog run ./cmd/symbolmap reconcile -type AgentSession -kind method -limit 5` |
| Current exported Go declarations and signatures | `go -C _catalog run ./cmd/symbolmap go -symbol agent.Session -limit 5` |
| Unreviewed declarations for a specific type | `go -C _catalog run ./cmd/symbolmap reconcile -state unreviewed -type AgentSession -limit 5` |
| Recorded partial or unmapped assessments | `go -C _catalog run ./cmd/symbolmap gaps -type AgentSession -limit 5` |

`mappings` includes assessed leaves and extracted unreviewed placeholders by default; use `-assessed` for reviewed outcomes. `go-only` searches separately reviewed Go-specific APIs. For declaration discovery, use `reconcile` **without `-assessed` or status/state filters** so both reviewed and unreviewed APIs remain visible; use `-state unreviewed` only for the review queue. `gaps` always excludes unreviewed placeholders and selects assessed `partial`/`unmapped` leaves. `go` reads the Go module independently of the catalog. `changes -old-root <checkout>` compares structural Go APIs without changing either assessment section; retain compatible additions and review source diffs for behavior.

For assessed counts, use `mappings -assessed -summary` or `reconcile -assessed -summary`. For all declarations, omit `-assessed`; mapping summaries include an optional `unreviewed_symbols` count. `mappings`, `gaps`, and `reconcile` accept `-assessed`. `reconcile` and `tests` read only the catalog selected by `-file`, with no `-inventory` flag. There is no standalone `summary` command. Flags follow the subcommand; use its `-help` to check supported options.

## 2. Resolve the exact declaration

- `-namespace`, `-type`, and `-symbol` are case-insensitive **substring** filters, not exact matches. Combine them with `-kind` when needed, quote names containing generics or spaces, and inspect the returned declaring namespace and full overload. `-symbol` also searches Go snippets and targets. Inherited members belong to their declaring base type.
- Every API method key includes ` -> ReturnType`, including `void`, declared async wrappers, and method-generic returns; do not unwrap async returns. Constructor keys, property keys, and test names remain unchanged.
- JSON is the default: read `mappings` for catalog results, `rows` for reconciliation, and `symbols` for the Go index. Pages default to 20 rows; the examples request five. Follow `page.next_offset` with the same filters and limit while inputs remain unchanged. Stop when the requested declaration is resolved; traverse all pages only for an exhaustive request. Use `-limit=0` only for a requested full export. Summary counts cover all filtered matches and reject paging flags.
- If a mapping query has `page.total: 0`, check `go-only` for a Go symbol and `reconcile` for the containing .NET type without `-assessed` or status/state filters, then broaden the query and check declaring ownership. An empty page with a nonzero total can mean the offset is past the end; retry at offset zero. Neither case proves an API is absent from Go.
- Treat command failure separately from zero matches: inspect stderr and the exit status. `go` and `reconcile` index offline and require cached SDK dependencies, prepared with `go mod download` from the repository root. Tooling dependencies are separately prepared with `go -C _catalog mod download`; `go-tests` is static and does not load SDK dependencies. If indexing is unavailable, use scoped source/data reads and label what remains unvalidated; do not alter dependencies or run extraction merely to answer a lookup.

## 3. Verify evidence and answer

- Read `status` and any `note` for the exact assessed leaf; `mapped` entries normally omit redundant notes. An extraction-added `unreviewed: true` placeholder stores `status: unmapped`, empty `go_symbols`, an empty non-property `go`, and no `note`; it is not an assessed gap. For assessed leaves, `go_symbols` records counterparts and `go` is illustrative code, not a standalone program. Free variables are allowed and their receiver/argument types are not fully checked. Verify Go signatures and actual callers before using a snippet in an implementation. Properties intentionally have no example.
- Reconciliation `state` is not mapping `status`: `linked` means assessment references and targets resolve, not implementation or behavioral parity; `unreviewed` means no assessment and its report status is omitted, regardless of the stored placeholder status. `suggested_go` is only a name-based search hint. A mapped type does not cover all its members.
- `go_only` records source-reviewed Go-specific APIs, not unmatched names or missing inventory coverage. Each entry contains only a concrete `note`; a type entry does not cover its members. Reconciliation checks these Go targets separately without adding .NET rows or certifying absence of a counterpart.
- The catalog's API extraction covers three core .NET packages, not every integration or external dependency. Existing out-of-scope assessments are retained without being treated as current extracted declarations; this is not a missing feature, and `outside-inventory-scope` is not evidence of removal. `go-outside-scope` means a target package was not indexed. Go results cover the reported build configuration, not every platform. An unresolved identity or unvalidated target is not a confirmed implementation gap.
- For a behavioral claim, inspect .NET source at the applicable recorded revision and compare the Go implementation, callers, and tests. The original `baseline` is historical provenance, not the latest inspection of every assessment. The catalog has no named review records or per-leaf review references; later inspection evidence belongs in PR discussion and Git history. Automatic placeholders establish no assessment against the baseline. Check `dotnet` extraction/build provenance, `review_source_changed`, `review_go_changed`, and Go dirty state before presenting an old assessment as current. The change flags compare revisions only with the original baseline, not a per-leaf latest inspection, and do not certify behavior. Missing change flags are unknown, not proof of an unchanged revision.

Answer concisely with the exact .NET declaration, recorded Go counterpart(s), and the relevant assessment or scope limitation. Cite source and revision for behavioral claims; distinguish recorded mappings from newly verified behavior. Do not dump the full JSON response or describe unreviewed/out-of-scope entries as missing features.

## 4. Update only when requested

- Change only the assessment fields of the leaf under its declaring namespace/type and exact overload. Keep `go_symbols` and `status`; normally omit `note` for `mapped`, but require a concrete explanation for other assessed statuses. Remove `unreviewed` when actually assessed. Preserve `dotnet` metadata, declaration keys, assembly/kind, and extraction markers (`identity`, `experimental`, `compiler_generated`, `unavailable`). Do not promote a name suggestion into a mapping without source evidence. Class kind and current scope membership are defaults; full reflection metadata is not repeated in the catalog. Add or rename declaration keys only through an explicitly requested extraction refresh.
- Non-property `go` examples use minimal calls or literals, conventional variables, and `new(value)` for pointers—not synthetic outer functions or unrelated fields. Real callbacks may remain. Property leaves omit `go` entirely.
- Preserve the original baseline; record newly inspected revisions and evidence in PR discussion and Git history, not new catalog review records. The extraction hash identifies the raw snapshot, not the catalog file. Never hand-edit extraction metadata or maintain another inventory, mapping, or count list in the skill. Only an explicit user request for extraction or refresh justifies `dotnetsymbols`; normal stdout is transient raw schema-1 `ecma335-v1` JSON with full matching metadata. `-update-mapping` refreshes an existing compact schema-0 catalog instead of emitting JSON, and `-input` accepts only cached raw schema-1 extraction offline; without an update it still emits raw schema-1 stdout. Refresh completes method return labels with the existing generic names while preserving assessment values; constructor keys, property keys, and test names stay unchanged.
- For a confirmed Go-specific API, use a canonical Go symbol key under `go_only` with only `note`, not an invented .NET leaf. Use `adapted` for equivalent Go composition. Go-only entries cannot also be recorded counterparts; remove an entry when its API is deleted or a .NET counterpart is verified, with evidence in the PR.
- Test identities use exact assembly/full CLR type/name keys with a unique Go test string or `null` when unpaired, never per-test notes or review objects. Pair only direct ports of the primary setup, entrypoint, cases, and assertions, with minor language-required differences; similar coverage or an analogous added subtest is not enough. Preserve existing Go test names, not CLR-aligned renames. Extractor refreshes preserve existing pairs. `go-tests` remains standalone source discovery, independent of the catalog; there is no stored Go-test review queue or classification list.

After API assessment changes, run `go -C _catalog run ./cmd/symbolmap reconcile -summary -check`; after test-pair changes, use `go -C _catalog run ./cmd/symbolmap tests -summary -check`. Run `go -C _catalog test ./cmd/symbolmap` and `go -C _catalog vet ./cmd/symbolmap` when changing the command's Go code, not for catalog-only edits. Strict checks inspect the whole unfiltered report, even with `-assessed` or pagination; a paged result or zero exit status does not establish behavioral parity or complete package coverage.
